annotations.text:
LuxePass — Epic 8: Admin & Support
The second dark surface of the system: same gold, same Bodoni and Manrope, same control heights as the Partner Dashboard — a different navigation, not a different language. UI copy in English.
The week continues Epic 7: it is Monday, September 16, and the case on the desk is the no-show The Ainsworth reported on Saturday the 14th.

Story 8.1 · One member, one case, one thread. Search matches a name, an email, a phone number or an LP number; the member record holds the bookings, the payments and the account in one place; the case keeps every message — system, member, partner and internal note — in the order it happened. The two ways a case ends are here too: change the booking, overriding the lounge's own rules if support decides to, or reverse the fee. Both are written to the audit trail with the agent's name.

Story 8.2 · The numbers behind the decisions. Every figure on these four screens reconciles: the fourteen bars add up to the 1,208 bookings, the 1,208 split into attended, no-shows and cancellations, and the revenue rail adds up to the net after what each partner is owed — The Ainsworth's $8,616.50 among it, the same number their own dashboard shows in Epic 7. Exports are anonymised by default and every schedule is one of those exports, saved.

Story 8.3 · What members read is edited here. A change to a lounge — one lounge or twelve at once — is drafted, then waits for a content manager who sees it exactly as a member would, side by side with what is live. Nothing reaches the app before that.

Seams declared, not designed here: the member's own view of a refunded fee and a moved booking is Epic 6; the partner side of the same no-show is Epic 7; membership plans, pauses and referrals are Epic 9. Roles and permissions for the console itself (who may refund, who may approve) exist in the navigation but sit outside the three stories.

Add a lounge · The same form stays open while the lounge is a draft — address and pin included. Once it is published the address is fixed: screen 12 edits a live lounge without a location section. Every photo gets an area name members read under it (15).

Add a lounge, partner included · The form that creates a lounge also creates the person who runs it: first and last name, work email and mobile. Publishing — not saving a draft — opens the partner account and emails the invitation (Epic 7, screens 13–15). The address the admin types is the one the partner signs in with.

Edit a lounge · replaces screens 12 and 13 (29 sept 2026). A live lounge shows everything members read — location and map included — locked; the approval queue is gone. Edit lounge (18) moves it back to draft: it leaves the member app, bookings already made stay valid, and it goes live again only when an admin publishes it (19). The draft form is the same one that creates a lounge: several partners, invited when it is published.

Partners · managed while the lounge stays live. Adding one (20) invites them at once — someone who already runs another lounge is just added. Suspend (21) is reversible and covers every lounge on the account; delete (22) is final. A live lounge always keeps at least one active partner. A partner who has not set a password yet can be sent a fresh 24-hour link (Resend invitation, 17).

Lounge adjustments · A partner runs one lounge: an email already used by another lounge — or by any other account — is refused with 'Already in use' (screen 20 no longer adds them silently). Partners sit in the main column of the new-lounge form and the draft; the form saves with 'Save partner' and closes, and 'Add partner' opens a new one (19, 23). Saving a draft and publishing confirm with a notice and keep the admin on the lounge (24, 25). Location is one column — address on top, the map full width below. Live photos are 144px tall and open full size in a viewer (26). The week starts on Monday. No 'Preview as a member': no story asks for it.

Lounge filters · The list is newest first. Live and Draft are quick filters: one press shows only that status, a second press clears it. The city button opens a search over the cities that already have a lounge — typing narrows the list, picking one filters the table and becomes the button's label. Status and city combine; Clear filters drops both.
